title: Apple’s new iPhone lineup to be unveiled tonight: What Sri Lankans need to know, and will a foldable iPhone finally debut?
byline: Apple unveils its new iPhone lineup on September 9, with rumours pointing to its first-ever foldable model. Here’s when to watch from Sri Lanka and what could be announced.

title: Four killed in four road accidents
byline: Four people were killed in separate road accidents reported in Kotawila, Matara, Koslanda and Keppetipola on September 8, police said.

title: WhatsApp 119 service for hearing-impaired
byline: The Sri Lanka Police have launched a special WhatsApp video service to enable members of the hearing-impaired community to lodge emergency complaints with the Police Emergency Call Unit 119.

title: OpenAI says it cracked 90-year-old maths problem in 88 hours
byline: OpenAI says it has found a solution to a decades-old advanced maths problem in a matter of hours using a new artificial intelligence (AI) model and thousands of AI bots.

title: Digital motor insurance in Sri Lanka: How to check and show proof of cover to police
byline: Sri Lanka Police has issued a special announcement to raise public awareness regarding the transition to digital motor insurance cards across Sri Lanka.

title: Hong Kong’s first post-colonial leader dies aged 89
byline: Tung Chee-hwa, Hong Kong’s first leader after the city returned to Chinese rule, has died at the age of 89.

title: Supreme Court nullifies special promotions granted to three police officers in 2010
byline: The Supreme Court declared null and void the special promotions granted in 2010 to three Chief Inspectors of Police, including a former Officer-in-Charge of the Beliatta Police Station, to the rank of Assistant Superintendent of Police.

title: Underworld figure ‘Konda Ranji’ arrested at BIA
byline: Organised crime figure Ranjith Kumara, alias “Konda Ranji,” has been arrested by the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) following his deportation from Dubai.

title: US strikes Iranian oil tankers as Tehran targets American base in Jordan
byline: US forces struck five Iranian tankers in response to Tehran twice targeting an American warship over the past two days, US Central Command (Centcom) said.

title: India, Sri Lanka to exchange three key defence agreements today
byline: Three agreements covering military training, defence education and the maintenance of air defence equipment are scheduled to be exchanged during Indian Defence Minister Rajnath Singh’s official visit to Sri Lanka, Foreign Affairs Minister Vijitha Herath said.

title: UK flights resume but airports warn of ongoing disruption from air traffic outage
byline: Flights from British airports resumed early on Wednesday after a major air traffic control failure, but hubs ​warned that it would take time for operations to ‌return to normal after disruption left aircraft in the wrong places.

title: Banks have been asked to equip their ATMs with voice guidance, Braille keyboards
byline: Banks have been asked to equip their ATMs with voice guidance and Braille keyboards for the convenience of physically  challenged persons, Deputy Minister U.D.N. Jayaweera told Parliament today.

title: Construction of apartment complexes for plantation community considered: PM
byline: Construction of apartment complexes for the plantation community is being considered, Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya told Parliament today.

title: A five year plan to fully digitalise education systems already in force: PM
byline: A five year plan to fully digitalise the education system, including administrative matters, is already in force, Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya told Parliament today.

title: India, Sri Lanka reaffirm commitment to regional security, development
byline: India and Sri Lanka have reaffirmed their commitment to work together for the development of both countries and the well-being of their people, while strengthening cooperation on regional security, peace and prosperity.

title: Vehicle number plate backlog to be cleared within six months
byline: The Department of Motor Traffic expects to clear the remaining backlog and provide new number plates within seven days after the next six months, newly appointed Commissioner General of the Department of Motor Traffic, Vice Marshal (Retd.) Thushara Idunil Fernando said.

title: Child’s consent more important than ‘Good Touch, Bad Touch’, Child Rights Advocate says
byline: Child rights advocate Tushara Wickramanayaka has stressed that a child’s consent is more important than simply categorising physical contact as “good touch” or “bad touch”, calling for greater awareness of children’s rights and protection.

title: Nawalapitiya-Badulla train services to resume by December
byline: Engineers overseeing the restoration of the railway line between Great Western and Nanuoya railway stations expect to complete the reconstruction work by December this year, paving the way for the resumption of train services between Nawalapitiya and Badulla.

title: Namal can’t be compared to a beggar: Herath hits back at Gammanpila
byline: Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath who briefed the Cabinet weekly briefing today rejected former MP Udaya Gammanpila’s comparison of the alleged payment received by SLPP National Organiser and MP Namal Rajapaksa as giving money to a beggar.

title: Helicopter carrying 5, including medical staff, crashes In Malaysia
byline: A ’’flying doctor service’’ helicopter carrying five people, including medical staff, crashed in Malaysia on Tuesday near an airport on Borneo island, authorities said.

title: Uproar in Parliament after Leader of the House makes remark
byline: Parliament descended into an uproar a while ago after Leader of the House Bimal Ratnayake told the Minister to construct a home for destitute opposition politicians.

title: Cancer patients in limbo as vital treatment disrupted
byline: Cancer patients awaiting radiation therapy are facing further delays as the CT simulation service required for treatment planning at a major cancer hospital has reportedly not been functioning properly since April 28, leaving more than 1,000 patients on the waiting list.

title: Frontline soldiers sanctioned, LTTE combatants pardoned: Gen. Silva questions Western sanctions
byline: Former Sri Lanka Army Commander and Chief of Defence Staff General Shavendra Silva has criticised sanctions imposed on him by Western governments, claiming that he is not a war criminal and questioning why military personnel who fought on the front lines continue to face international sanctions while thousands of former LTTE combatants who carried out attacks, including the bombing the Airport and the attack on the sacred Relics of Lord Buddha,

title: Let tax be collected, without making compliance a burden
byline: Sri Lanka’s tax administration recorded a strong revenue performance in 2025. The Inland Revenue Department collected Rs. 3,221.55 billion against an estimate of Rs. 3,093.45 billion, achieving 104.14 per cent of the target. Advance Income Tax, including withholding tax, yielded Rs. 175.79 billion, of which Rs. 71.62 billion came from interest. These figures show that collection at source is an effective and dependable part of the revenue system.

title: Sri Lanka calls for conclusion of country-specific UNHRC mandates
byline: Sri Lanka has called on the United Nations Human Rights Council (UNHRC) to ensure that country-specific mandates are not treated as indefinite, stressing the need for periodic reviews based on clearly defined objectives and measurable outcomes.

title: ‘Ethera Diriya’ home loan scheme for expatriates
byline: A new home loan scheme named ‘Ethera Diriya’ is set to be officially launched tomorrow (10), offering affordable housing loans to Sri Lankan expatriate workers ranging from Rs. 500,000 to Rs. 10 million.

title: Environmental protection gets a grassroots power boost
byline: The Environment Ministry has launched a new initiative to strengthen environmental conservation and sustainable development efforts at the grassroots level by empowering Development Officers attached to District and Divisional Secretariats across the country.

title: Namal well aware of Parliamentary Standing Orders: Madugoda
byline: Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) National Organiser and MP Namal Rajapaksa deliberately avoided referring to his recent arrest during his speech in Parliament as discussing a matter pending before court would be sub judice, SLPP MP Chanaka Madugoda said.

title: Vipul Misra appointed new CEO of SriLankan Airlines
byline: Vipul Misra has been appointed as the new Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of SriLankan Airlines, effective today (9).

title: Bread weight under watch: CAA raids 118 outlets and bakeries
byline: The Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) has launched a special islandwide inspection programme to detect underweight bread and ensure consumers receive the correct weight for the price they pay.

title: Scam behind decision to construct expressways?: Chamara Sampath
byline: Opposition MP Chamara Sampath Dassanayake in Parliament today questioned whether there is a move to collect commissions from transactions connected with expressways.

title: New UN map shows the world differently
byline: India looks smaller on a map than its actual size, and so does Africa. Greenland, meanwhile, looks almost as large as the entire African continent when, in reality, it’s much smaller. For generations, this is the picture of the world that many of us have grown up with. It may soon look a little different the next time you open a map.

title: Vehicle fitness tests to become mandatory for passenger transport
byline: Legal provisions will be introduced to make vehicle fitness tests mandatory for passenger transport vehicles, with the aim of ensuring passenger safety, Commissioner General of the Department of Motor Traffic Vice Marshal (Retd.) Thushara Idunil Fernando said.

title: Opposition calls for controversial businessman Nimal Perera’s arrest
byline: Opposition MP Chamara Sampath Dassanayake said in Parliament today that controversial businessman Nimal Perera, whose evidence was cited in the arrest of MP Namal Rajapaksa, should also be arrested.

title: Air defence guns to be upgraded under Indian grant assistance
byline: The upgrading of air defence guns under the MoU between India and Sri Lanka will significantly strengthen the air defence architecture protecting critical assets in Sri Lanka.

title: Sri Lanka presents key fisheries policy proposals at COFI 37
byline: Sri Lanka has presented a series of key proposals on fisheries policy, sustainable management of marine resources, protection of small-scale fisheries and regional cooperation at the 37th Session of the Committee on Fisheries (COFI 37), currently being held at the headquarters of the Food and Agriculture Organisation of the United Nations (FAO) in Rome, Italy.

title: Brent crude rises above $100 a barrel as Middle East conflict escalates
byline: Benchmark Brent crude oil futures rose past $100 a barrel on Wednesday, breaching the symbolic barrier for the first time ​since July 24 as intensifying conflict in the Middle ‌East fuelled growing concern about oil flows from the region.

title: Green number plates legally valid for electric vehicles
byline: Green-coloured vehicle number plates are legally valid and should be recognised as such, Commissioner General of the Department of Motor Traffic Vice Marshal (Retd.) Thushara Idunil Fernando said.

title: Rajnath Singh meets Sajith Premadasa
byline: Visiting Indian Defence Minister Rajnath Singh met Sri Lanka’s Leader of the Opposition Sajith Premadasa in Colombo during his three-day official visit to the island.

title: UK flights resume but airports warn of ongoing disruption from air traffic outage
byline: Flights from British airports resumed early on Wednesday after a major air traffic control failure, but hubs ​warned that it would take time for operations to ‌return to normal after disruption left aircraft in the wrong places.

title: President approves extension of Rs. 25,000 rent allowance for Ditwah-affected families
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has approved a proposal to extend the monthly Rs. 25,000 rent allowance provided to families affected by Cyclone Ditwah until December 31 this year, Leader of the House Bimal Ratnayake told Parliament today.

title: WHO honours Sri Lanka for sustaining malaria-free status, tetanus elimination
byline: The World Health Organization (WHO) has presented a special official citation to Sri Lanka in recognition of two significant achievements in the country’s public health sector—sustaining malaria-free status and the elimination of maternal and neonatal tetanus for 10 consecutive years.

title: Oil tanker hit in Iraqi waters, as vessels get caught in US-Iran attacks
byline: A tanker carrying about 2 million barrels of Iraqi fuel oil was struck by a drone in Iraqi ​territorial waters on Wednesday, port officials said, and British navy-affiliated UKMTO ‌reported that several merchant vessels in the Gulf had been hit by disabling fire overnight.

title: Over 2,400 Cyclone Ditwah-displaced people to be resettled soon
byline: Around 2,422 people displaced by Cyclone Ditwah in Kegalle District last year are expected to be resettled soon, a government MP told Parliament today.

title: CSE extends decline as selling pressure broadens
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange closed lower for a second consecutive session on 9 September 2026, with both benchmark indices retreating amid broad-based selling pressure.

title: Sahasdhanavi power project advances with US$291 million investment
byline: The Board of Investment (BOI) of Sri Lanka has registered its Agreement with Sahasdhanavi Limited for the development of a 350 MW combined cycle power plant at the Kerawalapitiya Industrial Zone.

title: Parliament approves Chief of Defence Staff (Repeal) Bill
byline: The Chief of Defence Staff (Repeal) Bill, which seeks to abolish the position of Chief of Defence Staff, was passed by Parliament today (09).

title: Why India and Sri Lanka need a new fisheries partnership
byline: For India and Sri Lanka, the sea has never merely been geography. It has been livelihood, memory and civilisation. Fishing communities on either side of the Palk Strait have for generations inhabited a maritime world older than the political boundaries that now divide it.

title: Sri Lanka provides USD 1 million in humanitarian assistance to Nepal
byline: Sri Lanka stands in solidarity with the Government and people of Nepal following the Bhote Koshi River floods on 26 August 2026, which resulted in significant loss of life and widespread damage in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and other districts.

title: Late asset declarations: CIABOC sets September 30 deadline to explain delays
byline: The Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) has warned individuals who submitted their 2026 Annual or Post-Retirement Declarations of Assets and Liabilities after the June 30 deadline that administrative penalties may be imposed based on the number of days the submissions were delayed.

title: Atlanta-born Ben Shelton stuns defending champion Carlos Alcaraz in historic US Open thriller
byline: Atlanta-born Ben Shelton pulled off the biggest win of his career early Wednesday morning, knocking off defending U.S. Open champion Carlos Alcaraz in a five-set quarterfinal that ended at 3:30 a.m. and became the latest-finishing match in tournament history.

title: Mamdani releases records on toxic air in New York after 9/11 attacks
byline: Just days before the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001 attacks, New York City has released a trove of previously undisclosed documents suggesting government efforts to downplay – or even mislead – residents about dangerous air quality following the attacks.

title: Oil tanker hit in Iraqi waters, as vessels get caught in US-Iran attacks
byline: A tanker carrying about 2 million barrels of Iraqi fuel oil was struck by a drone in Iraqi ​territorial waters on Wednesday, port officials said, and British navy-affiliated UKMTO ‌reported that several merchant vessels in the Gulf had been hit by disabling fire overnight.
